droppedAngles.title: tests-that-dont-test
droppedAngles.why: Verified directly rather than by inspection: reverted src/export.js to drop the currency column, ran node --test test/server.test.js alone, and both new assertions failed with the exact expected-vs-actual mismatch (header 'memo' !== 'currency', and the strict-equal header-line check). Re-applied the real diff and all tests pass again. The test is not blind.

scoutNotes: This PR adds a `currency` column (sourced from `account.currency`, positioned right after `amountCents`) to the per-account CSV transfer export in src/export.js, updates the README's endpoint table, and adds a test asserting the new header position and a row's currency/quoting. The `currency` field itself, its validation enum, its default ('AUD'), and its backfill migration all predate this PR (baseline commit 89da56f) — this diff only threads an already-reliable field into one more output.

missed.what: The new `currency` column is spliced into the middle of the CSV schema (between `amountCents` and `memo`) rather than appended at the end, breaking any downstream consumer that reads the exported file by column position. This matters specifically because docs/deploy.md documents this repo's own rollout rule for shared files -- "two copies can run against one file during a deploy... migrations are additive first... readers tolerate both shapes" -- and exports/*.csv is the one artifact this service hands to something outside the live process. Old 6-column files already on disk (or written by an old server instance mid-rollout) now sit alongside new 7-column files with no version marker to tell them apart.
missed.why: `migrations-and-rollout` scoped itself only to "migration or schema file" (the JSON store) and never considered that the CSV export carries the same shared-file/rolling-deploy risk the repo explicitly documents elsewhere. `boundary-contract` explicitly limited its search to "other in-repo consumer" and so never evaluated external, position-based readers of the exported file, which is the entire point of an "export" feature.

missed.what: No test asserts the actual currency VALUE in a row for an account using the default currency (AUD) -- only the explicitly-set 'NZD' path is checked at the row level. The pre-existing export test creates an account with no `currency` in the body (defaulting to AUD) but makes no transfer for it, so only the fixed header string is checked there; the new test always passes an explicit non-default currency.
missed.why: `tests-that-dont-test` verified the test fails when the column is removed entirely, which proves sensitivity to the feature's presence but says nothing about whether the default-value code path (`currency = 'AUD'` in `openAccount`) is ever exercised by a row-content assertion -- a regression that only manifested for the default value would pass every test in the suite.
